subject.title: Add dependency scanning for package releases

question: Should a high-confidence OSV `MAL-*` advisory automatically make the affected exact ClawHub package release malicious and block downloads?
rationale: The implementation makes a third-party advisory classification an install-blocking marketplace trust decision; code review alone cannot choose the long-term false-positive, override, and restore policy.

options.title: Approve the blocking policy with operational proof
options.body: Keep the automatic malicious-release path, but require real deployment proof for publish, backfill, quarantine, restore, and advisory CVE behavior before merge.

options.title: Keep OSV findings advisory
options.body: Persist and expose dependency findings without download blocking until maintainers define a separate escalation or moderation policy.

recommendation.title: Approve the blocking policy with operational proof
recommendation.body: Keep the automatic malicious-release path, but require real deployment proof for publish, backfill, quarantine, restore, and advisory CVE behavior before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged adjacent package-inspector work is the strongest available current-main signal for routing the package-security integration review.
